precepts.text: Jubal was the father of all such as handle the harp: Cain's line handled music. They are behind all the music back then. Music is very influential, very powerful if it's in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is. And Tubalcain, an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron, which would be what? Weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment, and power over weaponry, warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing. That was Cain's blessing too. Nothing new under the sun.
precepts.point: Not Noah. Noah didn't. And again, in process of time, thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them. Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men: that goes back to Shem's line. Not Ham's line, not Japheth's line: Shem's line.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
Ezra says that after Adam transgressed, death came “in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Genesis 4 shows one of those lines: Cain's. And in Cain's line, “Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.”

Cain's line handled the music. They were behind all the music back then, and music is very influential, very powerful when it is in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is.

Then Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and brass and iron mean weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing, and it was Cain's blessing too. There is nothing new under the sun.

This is how “every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” Wonderful there means evil; they started to mess around with the daughters of men. And they despised the commandments, which shows the commandments were around back then; that is how Noah knew clean from unclean. The wicked had the music and the weapons then, the same as they do now, and it ended in the flood that destroyed them.

precepts.text: Seth was Abel's replacement of righteousness. Then began men to call upon the name of the Lord: when the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous is born within the evil, always.
precepts.point: Not Noah. Noah didn't. And again, in process of time, thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them. Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men: that goes back to Shem's line. Not Ham's line, not Japheth's line: Shem's line.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

precepts.why:
After Cain slew Abel, “Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel.” Seth was Abel's replacement, the replacement of righteousness in the earth.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Ezra says the nations that came out of Adam “despised thy commandments.” When the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again.

Those tribes back then were called the sons of God. Tribes, sons of God: that sounds like the Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; wicked, evil leaders were around back then, and the righteous are around now. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous are always born within the evil.

That line carries straight to the flood. Ezra says God brought the flood on those that dwelt in the world, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That goes back to Shem's line: not Ham's line, not Japheth's line, but Shem's, the line that came down from Seth.

precepts.text: Thou leddest Adam into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward. Paradise was already here before the foundation of the earth; that is the rest prepared from the foundation of the world.
precepts.point: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief. Rest is entered by labour; that is the paradox the wilderness generation never accepted.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Paul says God’s works “were finished from the foundation of the world.” The rest is not something new; it was prepared before anything else was. Ezra shows it: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.”

Paradise was here before the earth came forth. Before Christ said the evening and the morning were the first day, paradise was already here. That is the paradise opened to Israel in 2 Esdras 8:52, where the tree of life is planted and rest is allowed.

So when Hebrews says the works were finished from the foundation of the world, it is telling you the rest was already created and waiting. Then “he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” That number seven keeps coming back: the seventh day Sabbath points to that rest God prepared from the beginning.

precepts.text: Thou gavest a body unto Adam and breathed into him the breath of life, and unto him only thou gavest thy commandment, which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds out of number, and every people despised thy commandments. The flood destroyed them as death was to Adam, nevertheless one thou leftest, Noah, of whom came all righteous men: not Ham's or Japheth's lines but Shem's, the righteous line of Seth, Enoch, and Lamech. When they began again to be more ungodly than the first, thou didst choose Abraham, whom thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will, Judith 5:6-9, who left the idols of his fathers, and madest an everlasting covenant never to forsake his seed; Jacob thou didst choose and put by Esau. At Sinai thou gavest the law unto the seed of Jacob, and yet tookest not away from them a wicked heart: the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed and was overcome, and so be all they that are born of him, so the evil remained; then David built the city, and its inhabitants forsook thee and did even as Adam, having a wicked heart, and thou gavest the city into the hands of thine enemies. The same cycle from Adam to Noah to Abraham to now: the righteous line gets the laws, goes off, is destroyed, and repents; the sons of God are not new, destroyed by water before and by fire next.
precepts.point: Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound: the law was introduced so sin could be understood and exposed, thou shalt not covet, thou shalt not commit adultery, to guide a naturally sinful people. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: keeping the commandments we realize how much we rise, fall, and stumble and how much more grace we need than under Moses, where animals could not atone for everything. That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men”. Yes, it passed upon all men; all nations are capable of sinning. The question is who God held accountable. Ezra tells the story. God “gavest a body unto Adam”, breathed into him the breath of life, and “unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed, and immediately thou appointedst death in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” The evil in Adam passed into all nations; Cain and them were wicked by default.

But out of Adam came a specific line God wanted to keep his laws. The flood came, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men”: not Ham’s or Japheth’s line, but Shem’s, the righteous line of Seth. They multiplied and “began again to be more ungodly than the first”, so God chose Abraham: “Him thou lovedst, and unto him only thou shewedst thy will”. Judith shows Abraham’s people left the gods of their fathers in Chaldea and worshipped the God of heaven. God promised “that thou wouldest never forsake his seed”, and “As for Jacob, thou didst choose him to thee, and put by Esau”. There is always that special line God deals with.

At Sinai he gave “the law unto the seed of Jacob, and diligence unto the generation of Israel. And yet tookest thou not away from them a wicked heart”. “For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.” The same evil that was in Adam passed on to the righteous line. Then David built the city, and “they that inhabited the city forsook thee, And in all things did even as Adam and all his generations had done: for they also had a wicked heart: And so thou gavest thy city over into the hands of thine enemies.”

It is a repeated cycle from Adam to Noah to Abraham to now: the righteous line gets God’s laws, goes against them, destruction comes, they repent, and out of that line the righteous rise again. The accountability for sin fell on that line. That is what Paul does in Romans 5: he gives the origin story of sin, how it killed off the chosen people, and why Christ had to come and die for that same chosen line.

precepts.text: Paradise, which thy right hand had planted before ever the earth came forward.
precepts.point: Time on earth began with the sun and moon on the fourth day, but with God a day is as a thousand years.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.” The waters under the firmament are the sea; the waters above are in space. There are different waters above the firmament: drink that water and you are good for eternity. Moses is writing in a similitude. “And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.” On the second day the firmament was created, and paradise, which is also called heaven, was created too.

The earth came after. “And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so. And God called the dry land Earth”. There was no shape or form down here yet. The earth was made on the third day, with the grass, the herbs and the fruit trees.

2 Esdras 3 confirms the order: “And gavest a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee. And thou leadest him into paradise, which thy right hand had planted, before ever the earth came forward.” Paradise was created in the beginning, but before the earth came forth, so it was made on the second day.

This is why the class kept saying Genesis has levels. When Genesis says God made the heaven, it is not only the sky over this earth. Paradise was planted by God's right hand before the earth appeared, and Adam was led into it.

precepts.text: The flood came upon them that despised the commandments, and Noah alone was left with his household, of whom came all righteous men.
precepts.point: The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
Ezra tells why the flood came. “And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments. And again in process of time thou broughtest the flood upon those that dwelt in the world, and destroyedst them.” This was the first time the Most High destroyed the earth for the wickedness that was being done. The flood came because they despised the commandments; destruction came because of sin.

“And it came to pass in every of them, that as death was to Adam, so was the flood to these.” Of them that dwelt in the world “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That is Genesis 7:23, Noah only remaining alive with them that were with him in the ark.

From Noah’s household came all righteous men: through Shem’s seed to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and through their line the Israelites.

precepts.text: The Most High breathed into Adam the breath of life; that breath is the commandments.
precepts.point: The breath of life is twofold. One is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen. Here everything on the dry land that breathed died; the fish were not touched.

note.label: Genesis 7: The First Rain and the Flood

precepts.why:
Genesis says all “in whose nostrils was the breath of life, of all that was in the dry land, died.” The breath of life is twofold. Ezra says the Most High gave “a body unto Adam without soul, which was the workmanship of thine hands, and didst breathe into him the breath of life, and he was made living before thee.” One breath of life is the commandments, which were given to Adam; the other is the breathing life, the oxygen.

Here in the flood, everything on the dry land that breathed died. The fish were not touched.

precepts.text: Adam was given the breath of life, the commandments, and a commandment to love the way of the Most High; the peoples after him despised the commandments.
precepts.point: The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Ezra goes back to the beginning: the Most High “spakest at the beginning, when thou didst plant the earth, and that thyself alone, and commandedst the people”. He gave “a body unto Adam without soul” and “didst breathe into him the breath of life”; that breath of life is the commandments. “And unto him thou gavest commandment to love thy way: which he transgressed”.

So Adam had commandments, and the law against eating flesh with the blood was among what was given to him. From Adam “came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number. And every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” The peoples after Adam despised the commandments, but the commandments were there, and they are still in place with Noah. The word is true from the beginning.

precepts.text: Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen; only Israel could leave the pattern of the law behind as a witness.
precepts.point: Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. That is why the memorial could stand as identification.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
The altar was “a witness between us, and you, and our generations after us”, so that if anyone ever said, “Ye have no part in the Lord”, the answer would stand built in stone: “Behold the pattern of the altar of the Lord, which our fathers made, not for burnt offerings, nor for sacrifices; but it is a witness between us and you.”

Why could that pattern stand as identification? “Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts; but not the heathen.” Nobody else could have built that altar to the pattern of the altar of the Lord, because no other nation was keeping the laws; only Israel keeps the precepts, not the heathen. The pattern of the law left behind is a witness that Israel was there.

The same thing is happening today with the northern kingdom. Our people left their own witnesses over here: the writings on the Los Lunas stone identify with the northern kingdom, and the traditions, artifacts, practices, laws, and books that are being brought out in the classes all prove our people were here long ago and that they are the children of Israel. Yet with all that proof out there, people still deny it, the very thing the two and a half tribes feared.

precepts.text: Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts, but not the heathen, who do not care about keeping the laws, statutes, and commandments.
precepts.point: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on and the innocent shall divide the silver; we do not want their Louis Vuitton, Versace, or Hermes bags, we want our kingdom back and the whole earth, because it belongs to us, plus what they took and some.

note.label: Job 27: I Will Not Remove My Integrity From Me

precepts.why: “Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts; but not the heathen.” The heathen do not care about keeping the laws, statutes, and commandments. Israel by name has kept his precepts, and that is why the just who “shall put it on” and the innocent who “shall divide the silver” are repented Israel. The wicked heaps up silver as the dust and prepares raiment as the clay, and it goes to the people who kept the precepts.

precepts.text: Israel by name have kept the Most High's precepts, but not the heathen.
precepts.point: The wicked hate instruction and cast the words behind them; when they saw a thief they consented, and when Babylon came to raze Jerusalem Esau was there saying raze it, partaking with the thief against his brother Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 50: The Mighty God Judges His People and the Wicked

precepts.why:
Ezra testified, “Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts; but not the heathen.” The heathen cannot keep the commandments; they never have and they never will. Israel by name kept them.

That is why the Most High asks the wicked what they have to do to declare his statutes or take his covenant in their mouth. The covenant belongs to Israel, not to the nations. Esau, seeing he hates instruction and casts the Most High's words behind him, has no business preaching it, and a new covenant for all nations is not what the Most High said.

precepts.text: Israel by name kept the precepts; the heathen did not, so a commandment-keeper is Israel.
precepts.point: Scholars themselves suppose from this language that Cornelius was a Jew or a proselyte instructed in the Jewish religion, because the pagan Romans worshipped the sun, the moon, and gods like Mars, Venus, Jupiter, and Hermes, not the commandments.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
Ezra asks, “what people have so kept thy commandments? Thou shalt find that Israel by name hath kept thy precepts; but not the heathen.”

Israel by name kept the precepts; the heathen did not. So a commandment-keeper is Israel. Cornelius, devout, fearing God with all his house, giving alms and praying always, is keeping the precepts, and that marks him as an Israelite and not one of the heathen.

precepts.text: The name of the Most High is found nowhere but in Israel, not among the nations.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“Weigh thou therefore our wickedness now in the balance, and their’s also that dwell the world; and so shall thy name no where be found but in Israel.”

The name of the Most High is found nowhere but in Israel, not among the nations. So remission of sins “through his name” is found in Israel.

points: Thus infirmity was made permanent. Definition read in class: an infirmity is a physical or mental weakness, frailty, or ailment, often associated with old age, chronic illness, or a condition that reduces a person's vitality. Was Adam feeling physical pain when he was first created? When Adam got cast down, and his descendants with him, then came the backaches and body aches and headaches; the woman now has the menstrual cycle and feels the pains of childbearing. When our father fell, we all fell with him, and now we all face infirmity, physical and mental weakness. Focus on the mental.
